passages.text: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
passages.sermon:
You are holy brothers.
You share in the heavenly calling.
Focus your thoughts on Jesus.
Jesus is the apostle we confess.
Jesus is the high priest we confess.
passages.original: Ὅθεν ἀδελφοὶ ἅγιοι κλήσεως ἐπουρανίου μέτοχοι κατανοήσατε τὸν Ἀπόστολον καὶ Ἀρχιερέα τῆς ὁμολογίας ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
God appointed Jesus.
Jesus was faithful to God.
Moses was also faithful to God.
Moses was faithful in all of God’s house.
Jesus was faithful just as Moses was faithful.
passages.original: πιστὸν ὄντα τῷ ποιήσαντι αὐτὸν ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is worthy of greater glory than Moses.
Jesus deserves more honor than Moses.
The builder of a house has more honor than the house itself.
Jesus is like the builder.
Moses is like the house.
passages.original: Πλείονος γὰρ οὗτος δόξης παρὰ Μωϋσῆν ἠξίωται καθ’ ὅσον πλείονα τιμὴν ἔχει τοῦ οἴκου ὁ κατασκευάσας αὐτόν

passages.text: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
passages.sermon:
Every house has a builder.
Someone builds each house.
God builds everything.
God is the builder of all things.
passages.original: πᾶς γὰρ οἶκος κατασκευάζεται ὑπό τινος ὁ δὲ πάντα κατασκευάσας Θεός

passages.text: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a servant in God's house.
Moses was faithful in all of God's house.
Moses served as a witness.
Moses testified about things that would be spoken in the future.
passages.original: Καὶ Μωϋσῆς μὲν πιστὸς ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ ὡς θεράπων εἰς μαρτύριον τῶν λαληθησομένων

passages.text: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son.
Christ rules over God's house.
Christ is faithful.
We are God's house.
We belong to Christ's house if we hold on to our confidence.
We must keep our hope strong.
We must not let go of the hope we are proud of.
passages.original: Χριστὸς δὲ ὡς υἱὸς ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ οὗ οἶκός ἐσμεν ἡμεῖς ἐὰν τὴν παρρησίαν καὶ τὸ καύχημα τῆς ἐλπίδος κατάσχωμεν

passages.text: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness, where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit speaks to us.
He says this message.
Today, you may hear God's voice.
If you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.
Do not be stubborn, as your ancestors were.
They rebelled against God in the wilderness.
They tested and tried God during that time.
For forty years, they saw God's works.
passages.original: Διό καθὼς λέγει τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς ἐν τῷ παραπικρασμῷ κατὰ τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ πειρασμοῦ ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ οὗ ἐπείρασαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἐν δοκιμασίᾳ καὶ εἶδον τὰ ἔργα μου τεσσεράκοντα ἔτη

passages.text: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’
passages.sermon:
God looked at that generation.
God became angry with them.
God said, “Their hearts always go astray.
They do not know My ways.”
passages.original: διὸ προσώχθισα τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ καὶ εἶπον Ἀεὶ πλανῶνται τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοὶ δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τὰς ὁδούς μου

passages.text: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’ ”
passages.sermon: God spoke with anger.\r\nGod made a solemn promise.\r\nGod said, “They shall never enter My rest.”
passages.original: ὡς ὤμοσα ἐν τῇ ὀργῇ μου Εἰ εἰσελεύσονται εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσίν μου

passages.text: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.
passages.sermon:
Brothers, I speak to you now.
You must watch yourselves carefully.
Do not let any of you have an evil heart.
Do not let any of you have a heart that does not believe.
Such a heart turns away from the living God.
The living God is the one true God.
Do not turn away from Him.
passages.original: Βλέπετε ἀδελφοί μή‿ ποτε ἔσται ἔν τινι ὑμῶν καρδία πονηρὰ ἀπιστίας ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ Θεοῦ ζῶντος

passages.text: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.
passages.sermon:
You are brothers in Christ.
You must encourage each other every day.
Do this while it is still called "today."
This will help you.
This will keep your hearts soft.
Sin can deceive you.
Sin can make your hearts hard.
Encourage each other so that no one among you is hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ παρακαλεῖτε ἑαυτοὺς καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ἄχρις οὗ τὸ Σήμερον καλεῖται ἵνα μὴ σκληρυνθῇ τις ἐξ ὑμῶν ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας

passages.text: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.
passages.sermon:
We have come to share in Christ.
We belong to Christ.
We must hold firmly to our assurance.
We must keep this assurance until the end.
We must keep the same confidence we had at first.
If we do this, we remain partakers with Christ.
passages.original: Μέτοχοι γὰρ τοῦ Χριστοῦ γεγόναμεν ἐάνπερ τὴν ἀρχὴν τῆς ὑποστάσεως μέχρι τέλους βεβαίαν κατάσχωμεν

passages.text: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to His people in the past.
He gave them a warning.
He said, “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
God told them not to resist Him.
He told them not to be stubborn.
He warned them not to act as they did during the rebellion.
The rebellion happened when the people turned against God.
God wants you to listen to Him today.
Do not close your heart to God’s voice.
passages.original: ἐν τῷ λέγεσθαι Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε Μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὡς ἐν τῷ παραπικρασμῷ

passages.text: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?
passages.sermon:
Moses led the people of Israel out of Egypt.
These people heard God's voice.
Some of these people rebelled against God.
Not all who left Egypt with Moses rebelled.
But many who heard God still chose to rebel.
passages.original: Τίνες γὰρ ἀκούσαντες παρεπίκραναν ἀλλ’ οὐ πάντες οἱ ἐξελθόντες ἐξ Αἰγύπτου διὰ Μωϋσέως

passages.text: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
passages.sermon:
God was angry with a group of people for forty years.
These people sinned against God.
Their bodies fell in the wilderness.
God showed His anger toward those who sinned in this way.
passages.original: τίσιν δὲ προσώχθισεν τεσσεράκοντα ἔτη οὐχὶ τοῖς ἁμαρτήσασιν ὧν τὰ κῶλα ἔπεσεν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ

passages.text: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?
passages.sermon:
God made a promise about His rest.
God swore that some people would never enter His rest.
God made this oath to those who disobeyed Him.
God did not make this oath to everyone.
God made this oath only to the disobedient.
passages.original: τίσιν δὲ ὤμοσεν μὴ εἰσελεύσεσθαι εἰς τὴν κατάπαυσιν αὐτοῦ εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἀπειθήσασιν

passages.text: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.
passages.sermon:
The people could not enter.
They failed to enter because they did not believe.
We see this clearly.
Their unbelief kept them out.
passages.original: καὶ βλέπομεν ὅτι οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν εἰσελθεῖν δι’ ἀπιστίαν
